QUOTE: "`ssl->MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(state)` becomes `ssl->private_state`. Public headers use it to rename struct members, so application code that writes `ctx->state` no longer compiles." and "although they are publicly visible in headers"
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer says opacity comes from renaming members to `private_*`, which makes direct access fail to compile, while the fields stay publicly visible in the headers.
